thread:
matt: heads-up — subtle resolution/typing failure when running our monorepo (pnpm workspaces) examples on multiple edge providers. builds fine in Node but edge bundlers fail to locate the SDK's ESM entry because of pnpm's .pnpm symlink layout.

matt: example error from Cloudflare Pages build: 
```
Error: Could not resolve '/workspace/node_modules/@redwood/sdk'
Caused by: Cannot read package.json for '@redwood/sdk' (followed symlink to .pnpm/.../node_modules/@redwood/sdk where package.json isn't being looked up)
```

zhang: seen this. esbuild/rollup-based edge builders either don't follow symlinks or only try to read package.json from a real node_modules directory. With pnpm the real files live under .pnpm and the top-level node_modules contains symlinks which confuse some resolvers.

elaine: two layers of issues: 1) runtime bundler can't read exports map so it fails to resolve the module entry, 2) TypeScript & LSP can't find the types because the editor's module resolution in the workspace doesn't map through the same symlink. That leads to runtime failing but also dev editor errors.

matt: I tried the usual list: alias the package to the dist file, set public-hoist-pattern in .npmrc, and add "module"/"types" fields to package.json. quick notes: alias fixes runtime for most edge builds, public-hoist-pattern fixes both runtime and TS but changes hoisting behavior for the whole repo. adding "module" helps older bundlers but doesn't solve types/LSP in workspaces.

zhang: we also experimented with a minimal shim package in the workspace root (packages/sdk-shim) that has a plain package.json (name @acme/sdk-shim, module/types pointing to a small dist that re-exports). apps depend on the shim instead of the original package. It's hacky but makes edge bundlers happy without touching pnpm settings.

elaine: FYI if you use the alias approach, remember to alias both runtime and types for editors: in tsconfig.paths (or use compilerOptions.paths) point @redwood/sdk to the dist .d.ts path, and in Vite/Next alias to the dist .mjs. Eg: 
```js
// vite.config.js
resolve: { alias: { '@redwood/sdk': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.mjs') } }
// tsconfig.json paths
"@redwood/sdk": ["node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.d.ts"]
```

matt: small gotcha: the exact .pnpm path includes the version and peer deps (e.g. node_modules/.pnpm/@redwood+sdk@0.12.0/node_modules/@redwood/sdk). Hardcoding that in imports is brittle. Use alias to the stable top-level node_modules path when public-hoist-pattern is set, or prefer the shim/wrapper approach.

zhang: for the SDK package we discussed adding a non-conditional "module" field and including the d.ts at the top-level types entry in published package so older bundlers and editors have a fallback. That change would reduce footguns. Filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/118

elaine: action items: 1) add a Troubleshooting note in developer onboarding listing 3 recommended patterns (alias + tsconfig paths, public-hoist-pattern .npmrc, shim package) and which providers they work best with (Vercel/Next, Cloudflare, Netlify). 2) propose package.json fallback fields in SDK PR to include "module" and top-level "types". 3) add short example repo under examples/mono-pnpm-edge showing vite alias + tsconfig paths.

matt: I'll open the example PR today and link DEVX-721. Appreciate reviewers who can test against Vercel and Cloudflare.
